evidence.exact_quote: PAT entry remains supported and mandatory.

evidence.exact_quote: Tokens and credentials are never persisted to redb, YAML, project files, or evidence logs.

evidence.exact_quote: Docker CLI and Buildx handle local build, run, login, and push behavior.

items.impact: Prevents late avoidable build failures and remote side effects during local build execution.

evidence.exact_quote: Chat, orchestrator, and Docker Manager UI can surface and trace the same build result.

items.impact: Prevents per-surface result divergence and loss of build provenance.

items.impact: Implementations may create duplicate previews, stop the wrong instance, or present misleading health and control state.

evidence.exact_quote: Existing repo selection validates reachability, local writability, branch existence/explicit creation, layout/migration confirmation, and unrelated changes/adoption.

items.impact: A stale or vague adoption could authorize mutation amid unrelated user changes.

evidence.exact_quote: Template-repo status row uses exactly one canonical state model.

evidence.exact_quote: needs_review clears only after regeneration or explicit user save produces all review-required fields and no unmapped-field warning.

evidence.exact_quote: Auto-commit is allowed only when the diff is fully contained within the PM-owned path set.

items.impact: A race can include unrelated user files in an automatic commit despite passing the earlier containment check.

evidence.exact_quote: Failed push preserves the local commit for retry.

items.impact: Retries may duplicate side effects or mark a remotely successful push failed, while a later retry may push a different commit.
items.statement: Push failure preserves the commit and divergence requires revalidation, but duplicate clicks/processes, crash during push, remote success with lost response, retry idempotency, and association with the exact commit SHA are not defined.

evidence.exact_quote: Allowed resolutions are user cleans the repo first, user explicitly adopts the dirty repo state, or user switches to another managed repo path.

items.impact: Builders can interpret adoption as blanket permission to fold unrelated work into managed commits.
items.statement: The allowed options are listed, but adoption does not specify what files become permitted, whether PM may modify or commit unrelated changes, the confirmation copy, receipt, duration, or revocation boundary.

evidence.exact_quote: Create-new template repo setup is offered.

items.impact: A setup path could silently create remote resources or leave orphaned local and remote repositories.

evidence.exact_quote: Maintainer folder defaults to DockerHub namespace.

evidence.exact_quote: Auto-push is configurable but disabled by default.

items.impact: Preserves safe remote defaults while keeping the local-to-remote handoff visible and user-controlled.
items.statement: Template changes auto-commit by default, remote auto-push defaults off, one-click push follows commit, and dirty, committed, and ready-to-push status is visible; detailed safety and transition rules are owned by adjacent units.
items.title: Commit and push defaults align with the detailed status model

segments.summary: Reviewed identity, shared receipt/blocked-state governance, projection truth, compatibility boundaries, and exact visible identity disclosure. Contracts are strong; cross-document implementation consistency remains a seam.
Reviewed remote drift and indeterminate outcomes, broad lifecycle detection, digest-first registry history, cross-surface ownership, Docker detection, and dual DockerHub authentication inputs.

Reviewed browser login events, credential custody, capability gating, repository API ownership, protected repository creation, Buildx preflight, and shared build-result consumers. Gaps center on login concurrency and capability freshness.

Reviewed preview controls, URL resolution, stream continuity, alert/trust ownership, enterprise host policy, approval preflight, and Kubernetes doctor checks. Gaps include concurrency, URL trust, stream limits, host-state precedence, and approval replay.

Reviewed active Docker operation anchors, event authority, publish side-effect partitioning, missing-repository resume, auto-push approval, canonical image selection, and tag sanitization. Operation schemas, resume idempotency, and tag validity remain underdefined.

Reviewed Unraid follow-on sequencing, artifact classes and provenance, round-trip XML editing, review gating, and deterministic XML emission. Major gaps concern path safety, missing provenance rows, merge semantics, and secure raw XML handling.

Reviewed Config mappings, field registry, unmanaged output, distribution rationale, generation and managed-workflow defaults, template-repo identity, and existing-repo validation. Concrete mapping, filesystem recovery, setting transitions, and dirty-repo adoption need closure.

Reviewed repository status and transitions, auto-commit containment, push retry, dirty-repo adoption, setup choices, layout defaults, and status UX. Critical negative-space issues are incomplete transition rules and TOCTOU/idempotency boundaries.

cross_document_questions: Do Contracts_V0 and storage-plan register every event family and persisted payload required by CRAU-015, CRAU-021, CRAU-027, CRAU-039, CRAU-042, CRAU-043, and CRAU-044 with the same terminal and blocked semantics?

Do Permissions_System and UI_Command_Catalog bind preflight snapshots, approvals, replay protection, allowed action ids, and policy-blocked outcomes consistently for Docker, registry, Unraid, and Kubernetes mutations?
Does FinalGUISpec expose exact requested/effective identity, disabled reasons, cached-state freshness, needs_review, repository status, and recovery CTA semantics without creating separate truth?
Do GitHub Integration and Source Control preserve the declared ownership split for workflow runs, secrets, commit messages, enterprise host policy, and template-repository remote operations?
